frameworks.name: Information-Based Buyer Spectrum
frameworks.definition: Buyers exist on a spectrum from low to high information rather than categorical emotional vs. logical types; all buyers move in one direction only (toward more information) and require enough data points to commit.

frameworks.name: Advertising as Information Provision
frameworks.definition: Advertising and outbound communication exist to provide enough information for a buyer to make a decision; the volume of information required is inversely proportional to brand strength.

claims.text: The distinction between 'logical buyers' and 'emotional buyers' is a mischaracterization. Instead, buyers exist on a spectrum from low information to high information; individuals start at different points on this spectrum based on their history of making fast vs. slow decisions, but all buyers move in only one direction—toward higher information.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
bounded_by: The framework applies to all buyer types regardless of industry
Does not categorize buyers as inherently emotional or logical

claims.text: Buyer decision speed is determined by reinforcement history: people who have been reinforced for making fast decisions start higher on the information spectrum, while people who were burned early on by fast decisions start lower and require more information before deciding.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Reinforcement history determines decision speed; positive reinforcement for fast decisions or negative reinforcement for hasty decisions shapes the starting point on the information spectrum.

claims.text: In a broad marketplace, only a tiny percentage of people have been educated enough to be ready for immediate purchase; the majority need multiple touchpoints to accumulate enough information to decide.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

numbers.axis: percentage of market with sufficient information at any given time

anchors.region: require multiple touchpoints to accumulate information

bounded_by: Does not apply to highly filtered or pre-qualified audiences

claims.text: The purpose of advertising and outbound communication is to provide buyers with enough information to make a decision; the volume of information required is the single lever advertising controls.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: A strong brand enables founders to compress the sales cycle by conducting multiple information-delivery conversations simultaneously: a founder with a large brand can have conversation one with 1,000 people, conversation two with 1,000 people, conversation three with 1,000 people in parallel, whereas an outbound-dependent founder must sequence conversations serially (one, two, three with the same prospect).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Brand provides pre-education and trust, allowing parallel information delivery at scale; without brand, each prospect must be taken through a sequential information ladder.

numbers.axis: information delivery efficiency: serial vs. parallel conversations

anchors.value: 1,000 people × multiple conversation stages in parallel
one prospect × multiple sequential conversation stages

bounded_by: Assumes the brand founder has large existing audience
Does not apply to new founders without established brand

claims.text: Outbound communication is difficult at scale because it requires taking each prospect from a low information state through multiple conversations sequentially before they accumulate enough information to decide; brand and good advertising solve this by doing the information work upfront.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Outbound requires serial sequencing (conversation one, two, three, four before decision); brand pre-educates prospects so outbound can transition directly to close conversations, increasing efficiency.
bounded_by: Does not apply to warm or referral-based channels
Less applicable once founder has established strong brand

examples.text: Alex Hormozi illustrates the difference between brand-driven and outbound-driven acquisition with a mathematical example: a well-known founder (with strong brand) can conduct conversation one with 1,000 people, conversation two with 1,000 different people, conversation three with 1,000 additional people—all in parallel. The outbound team then conducts only conversations four and five to close. By contrast, an outbound-only founder must conduct all five conversations sequentially with each individual prospect. The brand-driven model appears visually much larger in terms of total market reach because the information work is distributed across many parallel streams.

practices.text: Use advertising and outbound messaging to provide prospects with enough information to make a decision; calculate the volume of information required based on the prospect's starting point on the information spectrum.
Structure cold outreach campaigns to sequence prospects through multiple information-delivery conversations (conversation one, two, three, four) before attempting to close.
